$comment: Committed thresholds for the observer-effect budget. See bench/README.md for how to change one.
environment: Apple Silicon, headless Chromium, no CPU throttling

observerEffect.rationale: Interaction latency is the metric the footer makes a claim about. Two milliseconds is below the 8ms quantum Chrome reports INP in, so any real regression shows up as a whole quantum.
The fixture blocks for 240ms of its own accord. Five milliseconds on top is roughly 2% and still far below what a developer could perceive.
The pill is fixed-position and `contain: layout paint style`, so its correct contribution is exactly zero. The threshold exists only to absorb float noise.

Half a task per run means a regression that adds a long task to even one run in two fails. Attributing a long task to d0bar specifically needs long-animation-frame script attribution, which arrives with add-self-attribution.

Reported, not gated. The 4ms difference is the host's own request for the bundle, which a host pays deliberately. LCP on this fixture is dominated by a fixed server delay and its run-to-run spread is wider than any toolbar effect, so gating it would be noise.

bundle.rationale: Stage 1 as shipped: observers, ring, interning, vitals accumulation and the pill. The 2 kB figure in the original proposal was written before any code existed and was not attainable with the pill included. Rose from 4.09 kB when minification moved out of Vite and into an explicit plugin for both formats: terser normalises its options object in place, so a shared literal leaked the ES pass's `module: true` into the IIFE pass and silently deleted the `D0bar` global. Keeping the global costs top-level mangling. Deferring the pill behind a post-settle dynamic import would restore a ~1.7 kB critical path; that is a real option, not a decision taken here. Threshold raised from 4.5 kB to 5 kB by explicit decision, to leave headroom for the stage-2 boundary and the epoch column rather than have each increment relitigated.

The script-tag build cannot code-split, so it is one file by construction and is measured separately from the ESM build. Rose from 4.15 kB for the reason recorded against the ESM artifact; the build now fails outright if the `D0bar` global is minified away. Threshold raised from 4.5 kB to 5 kB by explicit decision, to leave headroom for the stage-2 boundary and the epoch column rather than have each increment relitigated.

Stage 2, fetched only on first open or by a post-settle background prefetch, so it is off the host's critical path by construction. Measured separately because it is a separate artifact: IIFE output cannot code-split, so the panel is built as its own ES module and loaded by runtime URL from either build.

bundleSize.raisedBy: add-vitals-view and add-otel-adoption, on the user's explicit instruction
bundleSize.raisedRationale: Raised on the user's explicit instruction, after being deliberately left alone twice. This is the number the product's central claim rests on, so what it now covers is recorded rather than absorbed. Two changes account for the 1.01 kB: add-vitals-view cost about 410 B for vital attribution (`selectorOf`, six module-level strings and the four capture sites), none of which can move to stage 2 because the selector has to be derived while the entry's element is still alive and the panel loads long after; add-otel-adoption cost about 850 B for tier 4's detection ladder, the span sink and the three new boundary methods. THE HONEST OBJECTION TO THE SECOND ONE: the sink is roughly 500 B of code that is dead on any page without an OpenTelemetry SDK, which is the overwhelming majority of them, and it is on the critical path because `otelSpanProcessor()` must be callable synchronously when a host constructs their provider — long before a dynamic import could resolve. The structural fix for the whole budget is still the one recorded below and still not taken: deferring the pill behind a post-settle dynamic import restores roughly 1.7 kB, which is more than both changes combined.
bundleSize.rationale: Stage 1 is the only bundle on a host page's critical path, so this is the number the product's central claim rests on. Unchanged by add-sw-correlator, which cost it 0.28 kB (5.49 -> 5.77) for worker registration alone; the join and the log read deliberately live in stage 2. Unchanged by add-requests-view, which cost it 0.48 kB (5.77 -> 6.25): the ring stays in stage 1 and the panel is given a window onto it, so the boundary gained `stats`, `read`, `onBatch`, `onVisibility` and `visible` — five object-literal keys that cannot be mangled — plus the resource-batch notifier in observe.ts and the visibility reader in phase.ts. The list, the virtualizer and every row's markup are stage 2. 0.25 kB of headroom remains; the next stage-1 addition needs a measurement before it is written, not after.

bundleSize.raisedAgainRationale: 660 B for tier 4's panel side: the four `OTEL_BLOCKED_COPY` strings and the two live-tier explanations, which are the tab's honest-degradation ladder rather than trimmable prose, plus the tier 4 join and the conflict path. Stage 2 is fetched at background priority after settle and is never on the critical path, which is why its budget can move where stage 1's could not.
bundleSize.raisedRationale: Raised after the trace view measured 3.54 kB over. Measured on this tree rather than taken from the agent's report, and split before raising: rebuilding with only the `add-trace-view` CSS section removed gives 14.31 kB, so the surface costs 0.73 kB of stylesheet and 3.19 kB of code. The code is a hand-rolled state machine and the span waterfall; XState was measured and rejected at 13.10 kB gzipped for the six imports the machine needs, which is larger than the entire panel. Stage 1 is byte-identical across this merge (6.66 kB ESM, 6.76 kB IIFE both before and after), so the trace view put nothing on the critical path. What this budget does NOT yet buy: the surface cannot reach its `found` state in a shipped build, because issuing the query needs a credential `add-credential-broker` supplies and that change is unbuilt. Roughly half the 3.19 kB is therefore paying for a screen no user can currently reach, and the honest options if this is unacceptable are to defer the trace view behind its own dynamic import or to hold it out of the bundle until the broker lands — not to trim the absence copy, which is the only part of it that runs today.
bundleSize.previousRaisedRationale: Raised by explicit decision after the vitals view measured 621 B over. Measured before deciding, and split before raising: of the vitals overrun, 190 B is CSS and 1.10 kB is code, and gzip had already collapsed the repetition — a pass compacting `format.ts` into a table-driven builder moved the total by 10 B, so the cost is unique English copy plus the DOM module, not duplication. The copy is not padding: it is the three distinct 'nothing reported' sentences, the `unsupported` branch that separates 'this browser cannot report it' from 'it has not happened', and the per-card accessible name that gives a screen-reader user the absences a sighted user reads off the card. Cutting them buys roughly 250 B and costs the honest-degradation ladder that is the tab's entire claim. Stage 2 is fetched at background priority after settle and is never on the critical path, which is why its budget can move where stage 1's cannot.
bundleSize.earlierRaisedRationale: The panel gained the view it exists for. Measured before raising, and split before deciding: of the 10.79 kB gzip vite reports for the artifact, 4.40 kB is the inlined stylesheet and 6.39 kB is code (size-limit's 9.83 kB is the same bundle re-minified by esbuild, which is the number gated). add-requests-view accounts for roughly 1.2 kB of the stylesheet — the shared column template, the trace chip, the four status tones and the waterfall's segment rules, including the hatched treatment that makes an unmeasured bar look unmeasured — and roughly 0.6 kB of code across the virtualizer, the row builder, the geometry and the formatters. None of it is deferrable: a requests tab that loads its own view on tab entry would put a fetch in front of the first thing a user clicks. Verified in the same measurement that no stage-1 code followed it across: `deliveryType` and `renderBlockingStatus` appear zero times in the panel bundle. Stage 2 is fetched at background priority after settle and is never on the critical path, which is why its budget can move where stage 1's cannot.
bundleSize.rationale: Raised because the panel gained a data path it did not have: the tier 1 <-> tier 2 join, the IndexedDB read of the worker's log, and tier resolution with its copy. Measured before raising rather than assumed - the four tiers' explanatory strings alone are 1,395 B gzipped against a 335 B overage, so the limit moved for content the panel exists to show, not for code that could be trimmed. The same measurement confirmed the worker-only log paths tree-shake out: `openCursor` and `readwrite` appear zero times in the panel bundle. Stage 2 is fetched at background priority after settle and is never on the critical path, which is why its budget can move where stage 1's cannot.
